posts.name: Demiher0
posts.cooked:
A vengeance fight this week. 

Proletariat, The Operative, Bugbear, Greezer vs The Wraith, The Naturalist, Legacy, Captain Cosmic in the Court of Blood

 

Your opening hands let you deal with most of the annoying ongoings iirc. I decided to go after bugbear first because I know the environment can block healing so his flip side wasn't so bad. (It otherwise was just a load of angry mobs. Good going Handelabra for playing up the communist uprising theme) 

MVP for damage was wraith with a 21 damage out of turn thanks to Dynamic syphon taking bugbear out of the game super early. Otherwise nothing horrible and a comfortable Mint with everyone in the mid teens

posts.name: Phantom92
posts.cooked:
A fairly comfortable Mint here as well.

Wraith did most of the damage, Naturalist tanked, Legacy buffed, and Cosmic added autonomous blades to speed things along. Greazer went down first, followed by bugbear. Operative went down next, followed by Proletariot knocking himself out at the start of his turn.

A rather aptly themed story for May 1st. Well played Handelabra, well played.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Easy mint, though I sure did make some stupid mistakes.

I focused on getting Naturalist set up as a tank, which meant that he initially went for card draw. He got Environmental Alies out before the first vampire. On the last turn I forgot that Environment Allies requires that he stay gazelle and the angry mob and some vampires dealt out some hurt to me. Fortunately all the villains were down except Bugbear, who was down to 5 HP, so it wasn’t a problem.

Wraith did 90% of the damage. She initially played Smoke Bombs, which was a big help in keepin the Constructs in play, but after that it was all knives for her. The Naturalist is the only other reliable damage dealer on this team, and he was too busy to go croc, ever.

While it’s easy to look at Wraith’s damage and count her most valuable, I think it was really mostly Captain Cosmic. Because he was handing out Cosmic Bracers to the Naturalist and Siphons all around. Those bracers made tanking with the Naturalist much easier, and the siphons meant extra attacks, extra damage buffs from Legacy, extra card draws for the Naturalist, and additional damage immunity for Legacy. Really they were extremely effective.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked: I felt that I was kind of low on damage output, and thus whacking Bugbear looked unproductive until Unhallowed Halls came out. The Operative just looked like a better target. Proletariat has his clones as meat shields, and wasn’t doing any damage anyway because the Naturalist had 2 DR and could tank him and his clones for no damage. I wasn’t sure if Legacy could hold off Greazer, so I put off taking him out until it was clear Legacy would survive. By the time I was done with the Operative, the environment and psychic self-damage had brought Proletariat down to about 5 HP, so he was next. At that point it was Greazer and Bugbear, and though the Halls prevented Bugbear’s healing, Greazer was still the much easier target.
